issues.description: Extraction unconditionally requires data/stories/manifest.json and story files, but the repo's data/stories directory is empty, so the documented tiny demo and integration test fail.
The only end-to-end test depends on missing repository data instead of self-contained fixtures or generated tiny stories.
Story loading has no fallback generation despite README claiming load-or-generate behavior, turning absent data into a hard runtime failure.
The HuggingFace backend is untested and relies on architecture-specific layer and tokenizer assumptions that can break across causal LM models.
Validation loads vectors and instantiates a backend from CLI config without checking that backend, model, layer count, or hidden size match the vector manifest.
Preference steering has the same missing manifest/backend compatibility checks and can silently run against mismatched vectors until shape errors occur.
Config loading accepts any YAML shape and performs no schema validation, so malformed configs fail later with unclear AttributeError, KeyError, or empty-data errors.
Extraction assumes non-empty story sets and will fail with opaque stack traces when emotions, topics, or stories_per_cell are empty or inconsistent.
Checked-in dosage output is flat for every dose, contradicting the claimed numerical modulation probe and suggesting stale or scientifically weak artifacts.
Checked-in generated artifacts reference a source manifest and topics that are not present in the repo, making outputs non-reproducible.
The default model load is not revision-pinned and uses minimum-only dependency constraints, reducing reproducibility for future development.
Tiny emotion detection uses substring counting, which can count accidental matches inside unrelated words and skew demo activations.
Dependencies are specified only as lower bounds with no lockfile or upper bounds, making test and demo behavior vulnerable to future dependency changes.
